crit: Main multi-class benchmark: 'Inspired by [8,13], we use the same 20 imbalanced datasets from the KEEL repository [12] as our experimental data' (settings follow MC-CCR [13] and MC-RBO [17]). Binary validation: 'To validate these noise-robust designs, we conduct experiments on the binary and mixed-type data ... we select ten common benchmarks that are also used in the three most advanced oversampling work: PA [5], FW-SMOTE [6], and SVDDWSMOTE [7]'. Simulated: four 2-D binary simulated datasets referred from [7] (SVDDWSMOTE), also used in 1-D form.
benchmark_inherited_from: [8] Koziarski 2020 (radial-based undersampling) and [13] Koziarski et al. 2020 (MC-CCR): 'the same 20 imbalanced datasets'; binary D1-D10 'also used in' PA [5], FW-SMOTE [6], SVDDWSMOTE [7] (supp); simulated datasets A-D from [7] SVDDWSMOTE (supp)
notes: minority_rule is a poor fit: for the 20 multi-class sets every class except the largest is treated as minority (KNNOR sentence p.6; supp p.13), coded as the closest option 'mean-size or IR threshold' (no explicit threshold given); the binary D1-D10 sets are named splits with no rule (would be repository-defined). crit_type own reason rests only on the binary/mixed-type validation ('To validate these noise-robust designs ...'); the main 20-dataset benchmark is purely inherited ('the same 20 imbalanced datasets', [8,13]). Source of D1-D10 not stated (KEEL-style names, 'common benchmarks'); binarised_by = repository because ready-made splits from prior benchmarks are used. Simulated datasets A-D are taken from [7], not generated by the authors (no generator described), so Generated not coded; 1D versions keep only one feature dimension (feature removal, no origin category). Table 2 (p.7) inconsistencies: Vehicle IR printed 1.17 but 218/199 = 1.10; Automobile #N 150 vs distribution sum 159; Cleveland #N 297 vs sum 303. Class distributions in Table 2 are unsorted. #Fn/#Fc split given, no total feature count. Main Table 3 baseline results (except KNNOR) are 'referred from [13,17]', not re-run.
